polymer.basis: Classification and typical values from polymer handbooks and resin data sheets, as compiled for the estimate model (docs/audits/2026-09-15-filtering-estimates-data/physics/). The document cited prints a density inside the range, not its ends. Celanese's sheet for Zytel 101L NC010 (R-CELANESE-ZYTEL-101L), a lubricated polyamide 66 resin for injection moulding, prints a density of 1140 kg/m³ (ISO 1183) and, on 2 mm specimens similar to ISO 62, a humidity absorption of 2.6 %, a water absorption of 8.5 % and 1.2 % after 24 h immersion, p. 3, with a melting temperature of 262 °C (ISO 11357-1/-3), p. 2. DuPont's Zytel guide (R-DUPONT-ZYTEL-GUIDE, SHA-256 4b28bc3c55f6...) prints 1140 kg/m³ for the unreinforced Zytel 101L and 101F, p. 6.

polymerEnvironment.agent: Water or aqueous solutions at high temperature
polymerEnvironment.conditions: High temperature
polymerEnvironment.finding: All polyamides take up water when kept in a moist environment. At room temperature this is a physical process which is reversible. Irreversible chemical damage to the material can only be caused by water or aqueous solutions at high temperatures. This is referred to as hydrolysis. Water uptake is mainly dependent on the amide group concentration of the individual polyamide type. For this reason, polyamide 12 is considerably more resistant to hydrolysis than polyamide 6 and polyamide 66.
polymerEnvironment.locator: p. 3 Hydrolysis resistance

polymerEnvironment.conditions: Not stated
polymerEnvironment.finding: They resist fuels, lubricants and most chemicals, but are attacked by phenols, strong acids and oxidizing agents.
polymerEnvironment.locator: p. 5, 1.1 Introduction
polymerEnvironment.notes: Statement made for the 66 nylons.

polymerEnvironment.conditions: Not stated
polymerEnvironment.finding: They resist fuels, lubricants and most chemicals, but are attacked by phenols, strong acids and oxidizing agents.
polymerEnvironment.locator: p. 5, 1.1 Introduction
polymerEnvironment.notes: Statement made for the 66 nylons. Zinc chloride is noted on p. 44 as especially harmful to 66 nylons.

polymerEnvironment.conditions: Boiling water (stagnant) and 80 °C aerated water tests; service life depends on temperature and oxygen content
polymerEnvironment.finding: Zytel nylon resins are resistant to hot water and steam. Thus, Zytel has found wide uses in such applications as hot water mixing valves, gears and baskets, equipment used for conveying in hot water and parts which must be subjected to steam, as in a sterilization cycle. Factors important to performance: a 15 °C increase in temperature may reduce life by 40-50 %; service life is shorter in oxygen-rich water.
polymerEnvironment.locator: p. 39, 5.3 Resistance of Zytel to hot water and steam

polymerEnvironment.conditions: Florida and Arizona outdoor exposure
polymerEnvironment.finding: Natural and pigmented Zytel nylon resins have only moderate resistance to the effects of sunlight but special weather-resistant compositions retain their properties and appearance for years. Table 5.05 Florida weathering: Zytel 101 NC010 (66 nylon, not stabilized) tensile strength 73 MPa initially, 37 MPa after 6 months, elongation 300 % to 10 %; Zytel 105 BK010A (light stabilized, black) 63 to 62 MPa and 160 % to 60 %.
polymerEnvironment.locator: p. 40 5.4 Weathering; p. 41 Table 5.05

polymerEnvironment.agent: Water absorption at 50 % RH and 100 % RH
polymerEnvironment.conditions: 23 °C equilibrium
polymerEnvironment.finding: Nylons absorb moisture from the air and 66 nylon equilibrates at about 2,8 % water at 50 % RH and at about 8,5 % at 100 % RH. This plasticizes the nylon, lowering its strength and stiffness but increasing its toughness and elongation. Moisture absorption increases dimensions of 66 nylons by 0,6 % at 50 % RH and about 2,6 % at 100 % RH.
polymerEnvironment.locator: p. 5, 1.1 Introduction

polymerEnvironment.conditions: 1.6 mm and 3.2 mm specimens
polymerEnvironment.finding: Zytel 101L: oxygen index 28 % (dry), 31 % (50 % RH); 1,6 mm 94 V2; 3,2 mm 94 V2
polymerEnvironment.locator: p. 33 Table 4.01 Flammability and smoke generation
polymerEnvironment.notes: Verdict convention used in this table: burns / UL 94 HB = not-resistant, V-1 or V-2 = limited, V-0 = resistant.
